title: Subscription or APIs?
author: fnaimi66
selftext:
Do you find it more worthwhile to have a $100 subscription to one of the big providers (Chat GPT, Gemini, etc), or should I just pay as I go with apis for frontier models? 

For context, I’m mostly modding existing games as opposed to making things from scratch.   
I call APIs from VS Code, but my last (small) mod cost me $30 in tokens for Astra, and a guy’s got to wonder of I’m taking the most cost effective approach here. 

Does anyone have any insight into this?

comments.author: Anadanament
comments.body:
Subscription, 100%. The cost efficiency of the subscription is literally hundreds of times better than buying API as you go.

Like, it's not even close.

replies.author: fnaimi66
replies.body: That you. I’m debating the Gemini subscription since Open AI is no longer accepting new $200/month subscriptions. Do you think Gemini is right for these kinds of projects?

replies.author: Anadanament
replies.body: I'd use Claude. Opus 5.5 is the best AI on the market right now. The second best is now probably Sonnet 5.5

comments.author: Free-Version-2746
comments.body: subscription is like 20x cheaper than API

comments.author: SweetKarmaz
comments.body: I have spent about $800 on subscriptions since I started (finally up to the 20x max plan now), but if I had done it via API it would be over $10000.

comments.author: SlashForward
comments.body: If you are going to pay more using an api than a sub, for example $25 API vs $20 sub. Then subs will always win as they will give you more usage for less cost. Well, this only changes of course if you only need $10 worth through API monthly, because otherwise a $20 sub would be pouring money away at a $10 loss since it resets monthly.

comments.author: reality_comes
comments.body: This isn't even a real consideration. API will make you broke.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: This is like paying for data roaming when you can easily by a subscription…
